summary: Your GBR monitoring satellite concept is well motivated, clearly written, and supported by literature, with a detailed week-by-week Gantt chart and STK tutorials completed. To reach higher levels, formally state mission goals, objectives and quantified requirements, correct the orbit error (GEO is ~35,786 km, not 600 km), add contingency planning and a consolidated source list, and present preliminary STK results with interpretation.
next_steps: Correct the orbit section: explain that geostationary orbit requires ~35,786 km altitude, and evaluate whether a LEO constellation or other orbit better suits GBR coverage and seafloor colour resolution
Add explicit, quantified mission goals, objectives and requirements (e.g. spatial resolution, revisit time, SST/bathymetry products) linking each to user needs
Extend the Gantt chart with contingency provisions for schedule variations, and compile a formal reference list of all planned information sources beyond the four URLs
Include preliminary technical outputs from STK (e.g. coverage simulations, orbit plots) with brief interpretation as evidence of progress
Verify statistics against sources: the 2017 bleaching figure referred to northern/central reef sections, not the entire reef

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly explains the GBR monitoring purpose, identifies marine and conservation scientists as users, and cites four sources — a strong Accomplished performance. To move higher in this band, formally state mission goals, objectives and quantified requirements, and double-check statistics (the 2017 bleaching figure applied to northern/central sections, not the whole reef).
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart with weekly tasks and deadlines, tied to the mission narrative (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, end-of-life), is a solid Adequate-level plan. The next level requires provision for project variations and contingencies, plus a consolidated, referenced list of planned information sources beyond the four URLs cited in the concept section.
criteria.C3: Your literature research and completion of STK tutorials 1–4 show genuine effort, but no preliminary results, calculations or STK outputs are presented or interpreted, keeping you at Adequate. Note the orbit error: a geostationary orbit requires ~35,786 km, not 600 km. Presenting early STK coverage or orbit results with brief interpretation would demonstrate Accomplished-level progress.
criteria.C4: Your report is clearly structured, well written, and consistently formatted, with a well-labelled Gantt chart — a strong Accomplished performance. To strengthen further, replace footnote-style URLs with a formal reference list so in-text citations and the reference list match completely, as expected at the top of this band.
